recommended.title: Auth integration decision
recommended.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam that the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: Candidate failover policy
recommended.acceptance: Retry and fallback behavior is bounded, deterministic, observable, and testable

recommended.title: Unknown media metadata semantics
recommended.acceptance: StreamCandidate can represent genuinely unknown videoCodec, audioCodec, height and bitrateKbps, and the media engine treats unknown as unknown rather than as a value: eligibility must not pass on an unverified codec, and scoring must not award or penalise a fabricated number

recommended.title: Show reviewers the full review surface
recommended.acceptance: The diff and briefing presented to a reviewer cover the same surface the approval will bind to; a reviewer is never asked to approve a fingerprint over files it was not shown; one canonical reviewSurface helper is consumed by fingerprinting, stale-review checking, the review diff builder and the briefing, and a regression asserts the file set shown equals the file set fingerprinted

recommended.title: Corrective, re-run: production rights-invariant breach in the watch route
recommended.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0703 and carries the same corrective forward under an honest review range. PL-0703 recorded implementationBaseSha f6c4b942ebbd02fd3fa9ed8f74fde4fc603affc2, which opened its review range AFTER part of the implementation already existed: the first incident repair at 9933a55 falls before that base and was therefore excluded from the range the first review was bound to. That record cannot be repaired in place. release is reachable only from CLAIMED or IN_PROGRESS and PL-0703 is in REVIEW; release deliberately PRESERVES implementationBaseSha even when it is usable; and reconciliation refuses any task that already records a base, because reconciliation establishes a base rather than revising one. The prescribed remedy is therefore to BLOCK PL-0703, preserving the false narrowed base as audit history, and to run the work again here. THIS TASK'S OWN BASE MUST BE RECONCILED, not captured: claim it, then start it with --reconcile-existing --base cf98b977b3c7c0113928bb9cc4d7fb6d02e802bd. That sha is the true pre-implementation base, being the immediate parent of the first incident-repair commit. Do NOT use its own parent b0b1dcf5a4826b763aa72d6375dd93e95a3aff33, which would widen the asserted range by one unrelated commit and make implementationBaseSha false in the other direction. The allowedPaths below are PL-0703's declared set plus packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/** and packages/provider-sdk/src/index.ts, because this round's corrective collapsed the two fixture providers onto the SDK's one and therefore writes there. The reviewDependencies carry over e2e/tests/media-rig.spec.ts and add e2e/src/env.ts and e2e/src/fixtures.ts: WEB_MODE and MANAGES_SERVER in the first decide the production-versus-development assertion, and TINY_DEVICE in the second is the probe that makes the unknown-height regression meaningful, so an approval that did not fingerprint them would stay artificially fresh after someone altered the mode classifier or the probe. packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/** is deliberately NOT also listed as a reviewDependency: it is a write path here, allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, and the validator warns on the redundancy.
recommended.notes: NOT ONLY A PROVENANCE REWRITE. At the previous head the reviewer refused BOTH security-review and rights-review ON THE MERITS, and those refusals are the substantive work this task inherits: the corrective had not reduced the fixture providers to one with the application consuming the SDK's, the runtime allowlist was not expressed exactly once with the SDK holding a witness it can neither forge nor classify for itself, the opaque rights-reference rule still existed in more than one place, a fabricated rights basis remained reachable behind a deletable condition rather than being structurally unconstructible in a deployment environment, and the two Playwright modes were not both shown as EXECUTED. PL-0703's typecheck, unit and e2e passes belong to that abandoned round and do not carry over; every gate here is re-recorded under this task's owner.
recommended.acceptance: Exactly ONE fixture provider exists in the repository, and the application CONSUMES the provider-sdk's rather than implementing its own: no route, no API handler and no watch-surface module declares a rights basis, composes a media URL, invents a candidate id or carries its own copy of the fixture variants. The runtime allowlist that decides which environments may construct fixtures is expressed ONCE by the application, and the SDK holds a witness it can neither forge nor classify for itself, so the SDK cannot admit itself into a deployment. The opaque rights-reference rule exists in exactly ONE place, with every other consumer importing it rather than restating it. A fabricated rights basis is structurally UNCONSTRUCTIBLE in a deployment environment -- unreachable because no constructor can be reached without the application-issued witness -- rather than guarded by a condition that deleting one line would remove. Both Playwright modes, production and development, are EXECUTED rather than only typechecked, and the gate evidence names the run, the commit and the per-mode results.
